The '''2024–25 season''' was [[Al Nassr FC|Al-Nassr]]'s 49th consecutive season in the top flight of [[Football in Saudi Arabia|Saudi football]] and 69th year in existence as a [[Football club (association football)|football club]].<ref>{{cite web |title=عن النادي |url=https://alnassr.sa/ar/about |access-date=3 June 2023 |archive-date=10 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220610063706/https://alnassr.sa/ar/about |url-status=dead }}</ref> The club participated in the [[2024–25 Saudi Pro League|Pro League]], the [[2024–25 King Cup|King's Cup]], the [[2024–25 AFC Champions League Elite|AFC Champions League Elite]], and the [[2024 Saudi Super Cup|Super Cup]].

The season covers the period from 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025.

==Overview==
This season saw the departure of [[Abdullah Madu]] who had been at the club for 17 years.

On 17 September, Al-Nassr terminated the contract of head coach [[Luís Castro (footballer, born 1961)|Luís Castro]] following a slow start to the season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Luis Castro Departs Al-Nassr |url=https://www.spl.com.sa/en/news/508368/luis-castro-departs-al-nassr}}</ref>

On 1 January 2025, Majid Al-Jam'an replaced Guido Fienga as the club's Executive Director with Fienga becoming the club advisor.

Al-Nassr sold [[Seko Fofana]] in the winter window for €20,000,000 to the French side [[Stade Rennais FC|Rennes]], making it the biggest sale outside the Saudi Pro League, although higher sales have been made within the league itself.
